answer: Each identity claims a tundra pond, locks a 70-credit bond and pays a fee. The claimant drills the ice with a spiral auger, filing the core under an onyx tag with thickness. An auditor re-measures the core on the public ice-strength table; error over 5%, a reused tag, or a key mismatch burns the bond. Fees follow claim order, not wallet: first 31, kth 31 + 6(k-1), 1000th 6025; 1000 fakes cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-auger ring fails: a borrowed core carries another key, and its onyx tag fails the re-drill. An honest keeper pays 31 once, recovering the bond after a clean epoch.
